I tracked the values segment by segment rather than line by line, because almost everything is a swap.

**How the swaps work.** Both triple forms exchange `a` and `b`:
- `TMP <- b; b <- a; a <- TMP` swaps them and leaves `TMP` equal to the new `a`.
- `TMP <- a; a <- b; b <- TMP` swaps them and leaves `TMP` equal to the new `b`.

So between direct assignments, only the parity of the swap count matters. Odd means `a` and `b` end up exchanged; even means they are unchanged. The final `TMP` depends on which form the last triple uses.

The counts below come from reading the triples in order by hand. They are error-prone for a list this long, especially the 324-swap final segment, so a single miscount would flip the result.

**Opening.** `a = 57`, `TMP = 36`, `b = 36`, then `TMP <- b` (36), then `a <- 43`. This gives `a = 43`, `b = 36`.

| Segment ends with | Swap count | After swaps (a, b) | After assignment (a, b) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `b <- 12` | 51 (odd) | 36, 43 | 36, 12 |
| `b <- 16` | 52 (even) | 36, 12 | 36, 16 |
| `a <- 93` | 52 (even) | 36, 16 | 93, 16 |
| `a <- 35` | 51 (odd) | 16, 93 | 35, 93 |
| `b <- 61` | 52 (even) | 35, 93 | 35, 61 |
| `b <- 5` | 52 (even) | 35, 61 | 35, 5 |
| `a <- 85` | 52 (even) | 35, 5 | 85, 5 |
| `a <- 55` | 51 (odd) | 5, 85 | 55, 85 |
| `b <- 58` | 52 (even) | 55, 85 | 55, 58 |
| `a <- 64` | 52 (even) | 55, 58 | 64, 58 |
| `b <- 31` | 51 (odd) | 58, 64 | 58, 31 |
| `a <- 64` | 52 (even) | 58, 31 | 64, 31 |
| `b <- 1` | 52 (even) | 64, 31 | 64, 1 |
| `a <- 91` | 52 (even) | 64, 1 | 91, 1 |
| `b <- 16` | 51 (odd) | 1, 91 | 1, 16 |
| `a <- 37` | 52 (even) | 1, 16 | 37, 16 |
| `b <- 52` | 52 (even) | 37, 16 | 37, 52 |
| `a <- 32` | 51 (odd) | 52, 37 | 32, 37 |
| `b <- 83` | 52 (even) | 32, 37 | 32, 83 |
| `a <- 72` | 52 (even) | 32, 83 | 72, 83 |

**Final segment.** I counted 324 swaps, which is even, so `a = 72` and `b = 83`. The last triple is `TMP <- a; a <- b; b <- TMP`, so `TMP` equals the final `b`, which is 83.

ANSWER: a ?= 72; b ?= 83; TMP ?= 83;
